correctness.rationale: The family has exactly \(2n+2\) distinct members for \(n\ge4\). For two distinct singleton members, common strict upper members are co-singletons and \([n]\), which do not form a chain of three strict inclusions. Every other incomparable pair in the family has union \([n]\), so its only common strict upper member is \([n]\). Every missing \(S\) has \(2\le|S|\le n-2\) and is placed in a copy by choosing two distinct elements of \(S\) and one element outside \(S\). The cited legs theorem applies to \(P\) and gives \(\operatorname{sat}^*(n,P)>n+1\).
